claims.text: The \(r\)-grassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) corresponds to the rectangle \(i^j\), where \(i=s-t+1\) and \(j=r-t+1\). [source-2@L1354-L1362|claim=formal-document]

With \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), set \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). Theorem 5.4 states that \(J_v\) is generated by either \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\} \quad\text{or}\quad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}. \] [source-2@L1380-L1402|claim=formal-document]

The formal conjecture is: “The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem 5.4 are both minimal.” The authors report computer verification for all bigrassmannian permutations with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1489-L1502|claim=formal-document]

Taking \(M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), the source conjectures that \(M/\Lambda_+M\) requires \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators and suspects the stronger isomorphism \[ J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}. \] [source-2@L1536-L1552|claim=formal-document]
